clue.text: Bring in soldier, perhaps, and material

parts.note: to bring goods in from abroad is to import them
a soldier is one kind of ant, so the insect is given by example

explanation.surface: An order to bring in troops and supplies, like a quartermaster's instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like a noun for supplies, but here it is the adjective meaning relevant or significant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a material point is a significant, weighty one that matters to the outcome.

clue.text: Dodgy sort of bag with no opening

indicators.note: having no opening means the bag's first letter is taken away

parts.note: a Jiffy bag is a padded postal envelope, a British brand name

explanation.surface: A shady remark about a suspicious bag that cannot be opened.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jiffy bag is a padded envelope sold under that British brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something dodgy is doubtful or of questionable reliability, the informal sense of uncertain.

clue.text: Back up expensive car — the noise it makes!

indicators.note: back here means the following little word is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce, a famously expensive car

explanation.surface: Someone revs up a luxury car and admires the sound of its engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back up' looks like a phrase for reversing a car; it splits into a turnaround signal and the word up.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth, contented low hum, as a fine engine or a cat makes, is the sound described.

clue.text: Guard's raised before son makes another sketch

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is lifted to read from bottom to top

parts.note: a warder is a prison guard; the 's is read as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A sentry stands up before a boy, who then draws another picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something again is to produce another sketch of it, the same idea in different words.

clue.text: Anxiety is no good, in a way

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviations for no and good sit inside the other pieces

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a kind of way

explanation.surface: Worry is pointless, in a sense: a piece of homespun advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the German-derived word names a feeling of dread or deep unease.

clue.text: This goes without his planning cover for house

indicators.note: the first word goes without the following one, so those letters are removed from it

parts.note: hatching a plot means planning it

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark about a plan proceeding without its author, and some house cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes without' strips HIS from THIS, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reeds laid over a roof form this traditional covering for a cottage.

clue.text: Swollen belly and oddly windy

parts.note: tum is a homely word for the belly or stomach

indicators.note: oddly here takes alternate letters of the next word, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A bloated, gassy stomach, an uncomfortable picture of indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks alternate letters of 'windy', I and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something tumid is distended or puffed up, often used of body parts or of inflated prose.

clue.text: Clothes worn by power party bosses

indicators.note: worn by places the following pieces inside the clothes, as a body is in an outfit

parts.note: togs is informal for clothes
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: Smart clothes worn to a powerful party by the people in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the people at the head of an organisation, those in charge, are its leading dogs.

clue.text: Poor ladies pimp used in a wrong way

indicators.note: poor signals that the letters are in a bad, disordered state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Women badly treated by a pimp: a grim scene of exploitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply something wrongly is to put it to the incorrect use.

clue.text: Giving notice, detective's not able to be located

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector; with the 's it gives DIS
something missing cannot be found

explanation.surface: A police officer is handed notice, then vanishes without trace.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing an employee means telling them their job is ending, so it is giving notice.

clue.text: Got on, looking embarrassed by footballers

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, the body governing English football
an embarrassed person blushes red

explanation.surface: A player managed, though blushing in front of the footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have got on, well or badly, is how one did or managed.

clue.text: They may take shots while propping up the bar

definitions.text: They may take shots while propping up the bar

parts.words: They may take shots while propping up the bar
parts.note: sounds like drinkers downing shots at a pub bar; really the uprights of a goal that hold up the crossbar and get hit by shots

explanation.surface: Regulars knocking back shots of spirits while leaning on the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is the football crossbar, and shots are attempts on goal, not drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The two upright posts of a football goal support the crossbar and are sometimes struck by shots.

clue.text: Wild acclaim if top becomes a foregone conclusion

indicators.note: wild signals the letters run riot and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: If someone comes out top, the cheering will be wild: an easy prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means a thing already done and settled, beyond change, so the outcome was certain.

clue.text: Most of close action destroyed breaker of images

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are wrecked and reassembled in a new order
most of a word is all of it except its final letter

explanation.surface: Nearly every close-quarters action wrecked: a battlefield picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last letter of close, and 'destroyed' shuffles CLOS with ACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal meaning: from Greek, one who smashes religious images, now anyone attacking cherished beliefs.

clue.text: Dazzle of news occasionally quashed by Star and Mirror reduced by these?

definitions.text: Dazzle of news occasionally quashed by Star and Mirror reduced by these?

indicators.note: quashed by, in a down clue, sets the selected letters underneath the other pieces

parts.note: the Sun is our star
a looking glass is a mirror

indicators.note: occasionally takes letters at intervals from the word, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Tabloid glare: the Star and Mirror newspapers squashing the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star and the Mirror are British tabloid newspapers, which the surface leans on; here they are a heavenly body and a looking glass. 'occasionally' picks E and S from news.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinted spectacles cut down the glare of bright light, the dazzle of the sun.

clue.text: Progresses smoothly from university during emergencies

indicators.note: during places one piece within the time span of the other, so inside it

parts.note: crises are emergencies

explanation.surface: A university that runs smoothly even through emergencies.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vehicle or a team moving easily without effort travels at a steady comfortable pace.

clue.text: Second very old church to support Bismarck, perhaps very quietly

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece is placed underneath the one it holds up

parts.note: Otto von Bismarck, the German chancellor, was named Otto
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A second elderly church backs the German statesman, all very hushed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bismarck is just one man called Otto, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase, literally under the voice, means speaking in an undertone or barely audibly.

clue.text: Parts of Oxford maybe fashionable, only small

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: Bits of Oxford University, perhaps trendy but tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is a lace-up shoe, not the city or university.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Oxford is a style of shoe, and the cushioned linings inside it are among its parts.

clue.text: Have on, taking in wife

indicators.note: taking in means the outer word takes another inside it

explanation.surface: Someone having a garment on, gathering in their spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to possess something is to have it as one's property.

clue.text: Ignore information rejected by the French court

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Facts dismissed by a French court are simply ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to disregard a duty or person is to fail to attend to them.

clue.text: Rising area is a regret for this land mass

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rue means regret

explanation.surface: A growing region is something to rue for the continent concerned.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the combined continents of Europe and Asia form one vast landmass.

clue.text: One may have sunk eight pints, full of energy

indicators.note: full of means the measure contains the next piece

parts.note: eight pints make a gallon

explanation.surface: A drinker downed eight pints and is now bursting with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunk' looks like drinking, but it means went down at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Spanish treasure ships of this kind famously went to the bottom of the sea.

clue.text: Fail to back up lease, depressed

parts.note: to let a property is to lease it
down means depressed or low

explanation.surface: A tenant fails to support a lease and feels gloomy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to disappoint someone by not supporting them is to fail them.

clue.text: People who may see vicars only at random

indicators.note: at random signals the letters are thrown together in no order; 'at' is also part of the letters

explanation.surface: Churchgoers see only vicars, chosen at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at random' looks like one phrase, but 'at' is part of the letters being shuffled and only 'random' signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychics claim to perceive the future or the unseen, so they see what others cannot.

clue.text: When scenery is an advantage

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a stage set is scenery

explanation.surface: A theatre remark: when the stage scenery itself is a plus.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a useful quality or resource is a benefit to whoever has it.

clue.text: Still single? This creature may not be

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
I, the Roman numeral one, means single

explanation.surface: Is someone still single? Perhaps, and this creature might not even exist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may not be' means may not exist: the abominable snowman is unproven.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan abominable snowman is a legendary creature whose existence is unproven.

clue.text: Part of farm that's British and a force at sea

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's force at sea

explanation.surface: A farm that is somehow both British and a naval power.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the large outbuilding used to store hay and house animals is a fixture of farms.

clue.text: Judges fool scattering roses across south

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stretch across the next piece, holding it inside
scattering the flowers throws their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool strews roses over the southern ground: an odd garden scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattering' turns ROSES into ESORS, and 'across' puts S inside it to make ESSORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: people who evaluate or appraise, such as tax or exam officials, judge things.

clue.text: Game played after love letter

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged piece behind the other one

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: played means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A game played after a love letter, a romantic courtship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love letter' reads as one phrase but splits: love is O, and letter is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the last character of the Greek alphabet is one of its letters.

clue.text: Inventor a large group backed

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so read from the end

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: An inventor finds a big group supporting him.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Nikola Tesla was the Serbian-American pioneer of alternating current and electrical devices.

clue.text: Stress coming after former partner gets part of the house

indicators.note: coming after places this piece behind the other one

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
tension is stress or strain

explanation.surface: The strain that follows a split from an ex, as they get part of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an add-on built onto a home to enlarge it becomes a room or wing of the building.
